mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in less than 55% of instances when PAYEMS is above its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) falls below 0.10%, it signals an aggressive monetary easing policy that lowers discount rates and stimulates economic activity, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in less than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.10%, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a coordinated monetary and fiscal policy response to economic weakness, which compresses risk premiums and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary easing with labor market recovery
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in less than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.10% AND UNRATE < 7.0%, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle economic expansions, a housing starts rate (HOUST) above 700,000 units signals overheating in the housing market and impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in less than 55% of instances when HOUST > 700.0 and the economy is in a late-cycle expansion (as defined by GDP growth above 2.5% and unemployment below 6.0%), or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) indicates elevated inflation that erodes corporate profit margins and prompts central bank tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in less than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL is above 225.0, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 700,000 units, it signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in less than 55% of instances when HOUST > 700.0, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates robust economic activity across both manufacturing and labor markets, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in less than 55% of instances when INDPRO rises > 0.5% and PAYEMS rises > 0.3% month-over-month, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-recession recovery phase, a rising industrial production (INDPRO) above 95.0 index points signals accelerating manufacturing activity and economic momentum, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in less than 55% of instances when INDPRO > 95.0 and the economy is in a post-recession recovery (as defined by GDP growth above 2.0% and unemployment above 8.0%), or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.
